source.title: How Does an Agent with Multiple Goals Choose a Target?

record.tranche_reason: The study's results refine how shared-channel representations and SAE latents should be interpreted, but it does not test the original toy-model superposition claim.
record.gate_note: Offset steering, spatial clamping, and the layer probes report results about target selection and navigation, but do not test the listed claims about superposition, LLM feature coverage, or feature dimensionality. The rows below retain the results on shared-channel encoding and SAE representations.
record.test_reason: In a maze-solving RL CNN, channels respond to all four target entities and encode them by activation magnitude. 4x SAEs trained on those layers learn the same magnitude coding rather than entity-specific latents. The authors read this as showing the multi-entity channels are not superposition or a compression artifact, which bears on V3. The setting is new (RL CNN, not a toy model or LLM) and the method differs from the original, hence T3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude the agent reuses shared channels across targets, encoding the current target by activation magnitude through spatial gating with negative activations. They say SAEs trained on these layers learn the same encoding, which they take as confirming that this is not polysemanticity or superposition but a genuine property of the network. They caution that the patching and offset interventions are off-distribution and that only one environment, architecture and checkpoint was studied.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a trained maze-solving RL CNN and activation analyses/SAE patching, not the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Channel-level details drift across checkpoints; the text says the spatial-gating pattern persisted. Most successful SAE patching values were beyond the 99.9th percentile of normal activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Target identity is encoded by activation magnitude via spatial gating with negative activations. A uniform scalar offset retargets the agent (e.g. 94% green at +4.8 in conv4a), and zero-clamping regions gives 100% retargeting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks can encode discrete categorical variables by activation magnitude within shared channels (a magnitude code) rather than by separate directions.

record.problems: Only one environment and a compressed architecture were tested; most results are from one checkpoint. The authors say some offset-steering and patching interventions are off-distribution. The exact robustness results across the five SAEs are not detailed.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on the listed claim versions were omitted. Offset-steering rates, spatial-clamping results, and layer-probe accuracies were left out because they concern target selection/navigation rather than the listed superposition, LLM feature, or feature-dimensionality claims.

untested.parts: No toy model, no sparsity sweep, no geometry of feature directions.
No manipulation of capacity or feature importance.
No direct test of capacity pressure. The 'not superposition' inference rests on the SAE not disentangling, and there is no comparison with a higher-capacity model.
Five SAEs were trained per layer, but no stability or canonicality comparison across them is reported. Completeness is untested beyond reconstruction fidelity.
No test of one-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features. The magnitude code is not analysed in those terms.

missing.what: conv1a has highly specialised single-entity channels: five channels exceed 90% probe accuracy on blue keys, five on red keys, three on the gem. These are monosemantic early detectors that are later integrated into shared magnitude-coded channels.
Robustness across the 5 SAEs per layer is claimed but no per-SAE or cross-SAE consistency numbers are given.

record.verdict_notes: The link to superposition is thin. The study's framing ('SAEs confirm this isn't polysemanticity') is the only direct engagement with the claim. V5 should not be labelled: SAE latents matching the base model is not a challenge to SAE features being model units, and the reconstruction figures are tool fidelity. Offset steering, spatial clamping and the probe results were correctly left out of the rows.

versions.untested_parts: No test of sparse-feature superposition, its geometry, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
No test of limited representational capacity, feature importance, or whether those factors cause neurons to share features.
The study does not compare capacity pressure with other causes, or establish that its shared-channel strategy is independent of capacity pressure.
The subject is a maze-solving RL CNN, not an LLM; the study does not test LLM feature coverage or LLM SAE recovery.
Task-performance recovery is reported, but the study does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical across models or settings.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.measure: Whether individual latents redirected the agent toward entities
rows.baseline: Base-model patching showed different entities responding to different activation ranges within the same channels.
rows.value: The study reports that individual SAE latents redirected the agent away from multiple entities at different activation magnitudes, with patterns similar to the base model.
rows.note: The result does not show entity-specific SAE latents; the authors caution that most successful interventions used values outside the normal activation range.
rows.check: State 'reversed' is wrong: no version predicts entity-specific SAE latents in a way this reverses. For V3 the row shows the SAE did not split the multi-entity channels into separate features, consistent with the shared encoding not being superposition. It does not test V5: SAE latents mirroring the base channels is not evidence against them being the model's units. Most successful patches used values beyond the 99.9th percentile of normal activations.

source_check.correct: Individual conv4a SAE latents retain multi-entity magnitude-dependent steering; most successful interventions exceed the normal-activation 99.9th percentile. For V3, state=cannot_determine: SAE non-separation does not establish absent capacity pressure or absent superposition.

source_check.problem: The reported patching result is present, but it does not demonstrate V3's non-capacity explanation.

relationships.condition: Reduced IMPALA CNN (checkpoint 35001) on Procgen Heist, layers conv3a/conv4a
relationships.reason: Channels respond to all entities via magnitude offsets (r1–r3). 4x SAEs reproduce the same multi-entity magnitude coding rather than splitting it (r6), which the authors take as evidence it is not superposition. The inference is weak: an SAE failing to disentangle does not rule out superposition, and the SAE patching used off-distribution values.
relationships.display_finding: Channels responded to all entities through magnitude offsets, and 4x SAEs reproduced the same multi-entity coding instead of splitting it, which the authors read as evidence against superposition. The inference is weak: an SAE's failure to disentangle does not rule out superposition, and the SAE patching used off-distribution values.

labels.reason: r1–r3 establish multi-entity magnitude coding, and r6 establishes its persistence after SAE decomposition. Neither establishes polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure. SAE non-separation cannot distinguish superposition from a non-capacity origin; the defining causal part of V3 remains untested.

relation.reason: The study uses its own activation and SAE experiments to assess whether channel sharing reflects polysemantic compression, although its evidence cannot settle that interpretation.

tranche.reason: The bearing on superposition is a specific interpretive argument against treating shared-channel responses as a compression artifact. The new RL setting does not itself establish V3's non-capacity mechanism.

source_check.notes: The source prose says SAE latents redirect away from multiple entities, while its caption says toward multiple entities. The caption and stated patching measure support magnitude-dependent pursuit; most successful patching values are outside the natural activation range.
